title: [DECODED] How Facebook pages used Kitty’s image to amplify Dutertismo
summary: Rappler’s analysis shows how digital creators and pages masquerading as news sites are using the former president’s youngest daughter as a vehicle to keep Dutertismo alive

blocks.text: Veronica “Kitty” Duterte has become a prominent voice in her family’s public defense of former president Rodrigo Duterte, now detained in The Hague for alleged crimes against humanity. Supporters celebrate her as a devoted daughter, ready to stand by her “Papa Rody.”

Circulating on Facebook is an image that captures this: the 81-year-old Duterte showing concern that he had “embarrassed” his family and Kitty holding his hand, reassuring him that his children remained “proud to be his flesh and blood.” This storyline has spread, feeding into a broader appeal for Duterte loyalty ahead of the 2028 presidential elections.

Rappler analyzed 260 public Facebook posts containing mentions of Kitty, published between January and October 2026, and found at least three clusters of narratives in which accounts shared nearly identical captions. Some accounts spread content across narratives, while others published posts appearing within short intervals of each other. The largest cluster, gaining almost five million views, centered on Kitty’s support for her detained father.

These posts foreground Duterte’s separation from his family, shifting attention away from the allegations of crimes against humanity he faces at the International Criminal Court (ICC). Duterte was arrested in March 2025 in connection with the ICC proceedings concerning killings during his administration’s anti-drug war campaign.
In his absence, Duterte’s children – Paolo, Sara, Sebastian, and Kitty – have taken up the mantle of speaking on his behalf.

The 22-year-old Kitty, Duterte’s youngest daughter with his common-law wife Honeylet Avanceña, especially finds herself at the frontlines. Her interviews and heartfelt posts on social media have supplied material for online accounts aiming to rally sympathy and support for the Dutertes.

Unlike her siblings, Kitty is a fresh face with no political track record to be judged on, which could make her appeal to supporters stronger, Arjan Aguirre, assistant professor of political science at Ateneo de Manila University, told Rappler.

“With Kitty, they’re trying to project the idea to the general public that even if you are not a supporter of the Duterte bloc, you have to sympathize with us because I am the youngest, I’m the bunso, and I feel sad about what’s happening,” according to Aguirre, who is also pursuing his PhD in political science at the University of Pittsburgh.

Kitty was only 14 when her father was elected president in 2016, while her siblings already held local seats in Davao. That distance from politics, Aguirre said, is what makes her the obvious choice to convey these seemingly innocent narratives.

He highlighted that Kitty’s image projects a gentler tone than her siblings. “Nag-bo-border pa rin siya doon sa pagiging naive. May mga persecution pa rin siyang nababanggit pero hindi gano’n katapang.” (She still borders on being naive. She does mention persecution, but not as boldly.)

More than half of the 260 posts analyzed pulled emotionally-charged quotes from Kitty’s interview with blogger Alvin & Tourism on April 20. Posting peaked the following day, April 21, just days before news broke out of the ICC’s confirmation of Duterte’s charges.
The same quotes then resurfaced in September, when Duterte made his first in-person appearance at the ICC courtroom since his arrest.
By October, the posts about the “flesh and blood” narrative had accumulated about 4.76 million views on Facebook, based on Rappler’s monitoring.

Behind those views were 78 pages and profiles that circulated the narrative. Rappler identified 17 pages linked to Pilipinas Today, a network of news and media pages operating across the country. An earlier investigation found that the group is run by Sartine IT Solutions, a political consulting firm previously linked to foreign interference in elections.

Alongside the Pilipinas Today network, some news-branded pages that had previously used partisan names contributed to the narrative’s amplification. For instance, the page News Ngayon – which accounted for 21.67% of the total post views in this cluster – changed its name six times. It was originally Duterte Latest News, when it was created on January 17, 2018.

Another profile, Venielyn Rahman, which categorizes itself as a news and media website, racked up a total of 110,075 views for the same quotes from Kitty on April 21. A closer look at its Profile Transparency information indicated that the primary location of the profile owner is listed in Bangladesh. The account, however, largely published Filipino celebrity content and political news.
It is among the four pages whose administrators are located outside the Philippines, including one based in Macau, one in Canada, and a second one in Bangladesh.

blocks.caption: OUTSIDE THE PHILIPPINES. Four pages had administrators located in other countries. Rappler screenshots

blocks.text: Other pages in this cluster hid their political purpose behind misleading names. The page Words of Wisdom: Inspirational Quotes to Live By, which has about 141,000 followers, claims to be “dedicated to providing you with daily inspiration, motivation, and positivity,” but in fact carries political content about the Dutertes.
In a second cluster of posts, Facebook pages cast Kitty as the messenger of her father’s supposed political support for protests back home, and appeared to cash in on this narrative.

At least 19 Facebook fan pages shared identical captions attributing the message to Kitty, accompanied by carousels that steered users toward the same affiliate marketing link. These pages accumulated more than 21,000 post views as of October.

blocks.caption: REPETITIVE POSTS. Facebook pages analyzed showed identical posts containing affiliate marketing links. Rappler screenshots

blocks.text: Posts spiked a few days after Iglesia ni Cristo’s three-day demonstration from June 30 to July 2 in support of long-time Duterte ally Senator Rodante Marcoleta.

blocks.caption: AFFILIATE LINKS. Facebook pages cast Kitty as the messenger of her father’s supposed political support for protests back home, then added links to an online marketplace. Rappler screenshots

blocks.text: Further inspection of 12 of these pages found similar blue checkmark edits on their profile images, mimicking the verification badges Facebook awards to premium accounts. Some of them also posted the same manipulated photos within minutes of each other.

blocks.caption: FAKE CHECKMARKS. Facebook pages found in Rappler’s dataset showed blue checkmarks edited on their profile photos. Rappler screenshots

blocks.text: For Aguirre, all these narratives position Kitty as a political force – even a potential successor – within the Duterte dynasty.
“If ever Rodrigo Roa Duterte is gone, who would emerge [a]s the central figure in the Duterte bloc? I’m sure Kitty will put up a fight for that,” he added.

The third cluster of posts echoed this push to keep the Duterte legacy alive through his children. Rappler’s analysis found copypasta messages across 29 pages and profiles in January, claiming that only the Dutertes could put an end to crime and corruption.

“Hindi sila basta anak ni Tatay Digong. Sila ang legasiya ng tapang, disiplina, malasakit, at paninindigang walang atrasan—kahit malalakas pa ang kalaban,” the captions read. (They’re not just children of Tatay Digong. They are the legacy of courage, discipline, compassion, and an unwavering resolve—even when facing formidable opponents.)

One post carrying this message, published by the page Parang May Mali, garnered 1.75 million views. The profile Boss Lee Vlog distributed it across seven Facebook groups, including communities of local buying and selling, hog raising, and religious discussion.

By July, the accounts in this cluster began to explicitly push for #Duterte2028. The Facebook page Kitty Duterte: Unofficial wrote, “Kung sunod-sunod na tatakbong pangulo ang mga Duterte, susuportahan mo ba sila?” (If the Dutertes run for president one after another, will you support them?) In the same caption, it answered its own question, “YES NA YES.”

According to Aguirre, 2028 could be the Dutertes’ year. If the vice president gets impeached, he predicted, whoever they field in the polls could win by saying the family had been persecuted and wronged.

These accounts suggest that the campaign has already begun. With Sara’s presidential bid in the works, these accounts have a clear pitch to the Filipino people beyond sympathy for her father: back the next Duterte. – with reports from Alex Culla/Rappler.com

Nica is a freelance journalist and OSINT researcher reporting on online information manipulation campaigns and tech platform accountability. Her work has centered on information integrity, previously fact-checking mis/disinformation and building news products at VERA Files. She is now pursuing a joint master’s degree in Journalism, Media, and Globalization in Europe. You may reach her at ndhanopol@gmail.com.
